description: NREL OpenPATH, formerly e-mission, collects consented phone travel records and turns them into mobility information for users and aggregate transport studies. The current backend repository README describes a Python REST server, database access, preprocessing scripts and separate phone applications; the project documentation repository explains the wider system. Users deploy the server, connect consented mobile clients and configure analysis; outputs include processed trip and mode information. Geographic coverage follows enrolled users and deployment areas. GitHub metadata states BSD-3-Clause licensing for the server code, while personal mobility data require privacy and consent controls. A limitation is that phone sensing can miss trips or misclassify modes, and the public code does not provide a general-purpose published trip dataset. OpenPATH can collect demand observations for transport planning simulations. The related AequilibraE catalogue model assigns trips to networks, not collecting them. No trip traces, server container or mobile app was downloaded.
name: NREL OpenPATH travel-data server
